notes: Checked at this exact model across a review and several retailer tables. 800R is the tightest curve on this list by a wide margin - it wraps noticeably, which suits a game and divides opinion for spreadsheet work; the work profile scores an aggressive curve lowest for that reason. Height adjustment is confirmed present (tilt -10/+15, swivel -10/+10) but no source gave the travel in millimetres. There is no USB-C at all: the hub is USB-A/USB-B, so single-cable docking is not possible and the usb_c field is a verified zero rather than an unknown. Burn-in warranty length was not established for this model and is left unknown rather than assumed from LG's other OLED lines. Contrast is null because per-pixel emission makes a static ratio meaningless; the scoring credits OLED directly instead.

Checked at this exact model; RTINGS measured the same panel as S34BG85 and reports about 120 mm of height adjustment and no swivel, which is the strongest evidence on this entry. G85SD is a separate, later model code for a similar monitor and is deliberately NOT an alias here: 'G85SB' cannot match a G85SD listing, so a G85SD in a shop will show up in Discover as the different product it is. Burn-in warranty is left unknown on purpose - sources flatly contradict each other, one reporting a US one-year warranty that excludes burn-in and a retailer relaying a Samsung answer about three years including panel replacement, and the terms are regional. Do not read the blank as 'no cover'. Response time is quoted at both 0.1 ms and 0.03 ms depending on source; the lower figure is recorded as the quote, and the scoring caps what a quote can earn anyway.

Checked at this exact model against MSI's own specification sheet: 240 Hz, 98 W USB-C power delivery, KVM over the USB 2.0 hub, True Black 400, and a three-year warranty that explicitly covers OLED burn-in - the only burn-in cover on this list confirmed in a maker's own document. Height adjustment 0-100 mm per MSI's store page. '341CQP' is deliberately absent from the aliases: MSI also sells a 341CQP without the X at a lower refresh rate, and a '341CQP' alias would match the X's title as a prefix and claim whichever of the two it met first. 'MAG341CQPXQDOLED' is a retailer part-number form seen in listings. VRR left unknown: the spec sheet section seen listed Adaptive-Sync support loosely without naming a certification.

Checked at this exact model, but from retailer spec tables rather than dell.com, which could not be opened from this session. 165 Hz is the DisplayPort figure; HDMI is capped at 100 Hz. The three-year burn-in cover is stated plainly in one large retailer's listing and more vaguely as 'three-year service coverage' in others, so treat the cover as probable rather than certain and confirm with the Cyprus seller. 'AW3423' is deliberately not an alias: the AW3423DW is a different monitor (G-Sync module, 175 Hz) and a shared prefix would let this entry claim its listings. A DW in a shop will therefore appear in Discover rather than being silently priced as a DWF.

Checked at this exact model against a full spec table read in its entirety, not a search snippet: QD-OLED 1800R, 3440x1440 at 110 PPI, 175 Hz, 0.03 ms, 250 nits, 99% DCI-P3, 10-bit, anti-reflective finish, 120 mm height adjustment with -2/+20 tilt, FreeSync Premium Pro and G-Sync both listed. It is 175 Hz, NOT the 240 Hz often repeated - that was worth checking, because 240 Hz would have been worth four more points under the gaming profile. USB-C is a verified absence rather than an unknown: the connector list is complete (1x DP 1.4, 2x HDMI 2.1, 2x USB 3.0, 1x USB 3.0 type B) and holds no Type-C, so this cannot dock a laptop. KVM is left unknown; the upstream USB-B is the hardware a KVM would use but no source consulted says it has one. The HDR field records what the source states, 'Certificado HDR: HDR10'. Its sibling G85SB carries DisplayHDR True Black 400 and this model very likely does too, but it was not confirmed, so the HDR band here is probably understated by four points rather than overstated. Added because the live Discover scan found it stocked in Cyprus at 899 EUR and 1,399 EUR in two shops on the same day.
